# Expose workbench last-activity data for console consumption

## Description

The notebook controller already tracks per-workbench last-activity (the idle culler probes the Jupyter server API per kernel), but that information is internal to the controller and is not available to the RHOAI web console, which reads Kubernetes resources and owns no data plane. This epic makes the notebook controller's last-activity tracking consumable by the web console so that an idle-workbench report can be built on top of it.

## Scope

- Surface per-workbench last-activity timestamps from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking in a form the RHOAI web console can read per project (the exact interface — e.g., status fields on the workbench resource or another console-readable mechanism — is decided by the implementing team).
- Ensure the per-workbench owner and reserved-resource information needed for an idle-workbench report is readable by the console (expected to be already available from existing workbench resources; verify and fill any gap found).
- Preserve existing idle-culler behavior — the change must not alter culling decisions or defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with workbenches that have varying recent activity, the per-workbench last-activity timestamp maintained by the notebook controller is retrievable by the web console for each workbench in that project.
- The surfaced activity values match the controller's internally tracked activity data (validated against the culler's view for a sample of active and idle workbenches).
- Existing idle-culling behavior is unchanged: culling thresholds, defaults, and per-workbench overrides behave exactly as before the change.
- The notebook controller's build and test pipeline is green with the change.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking — this epic delivers the sourced activity data.

# Idle and stale resource reports in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers the admin-facing idle resource reporting in the RHOAI web console: a per-project idle-workbench report and a per-project stale pipeline-run report, with CSV export for either report. It gives cluster administrators a single place to see which resources are sitting idle so they can reclaim capacity with confidence.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console showing, per workbench: last activity (sourced from the notebook controller's activity data), owner, and reserved resources.
- Per-project stale pipeline-run report showing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age that have retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Configurable age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report.
- Read-only reporting — no automated reclamation or deletion (explicitly out of scope in the strategy), and no cost/chargeback calculations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity, the console displays an idle-workbench report listing each workbench's last activity, owner, and reserved resources, and the values match the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of varying age with retained artifacts, the console displays a stale pipeline-run report listing the runs older than the configured age, and the entries match Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- The stale-run age threshold is configurable and the report reflects changes to it without code changes.
- Either report can be exported as CSV and the export contains the same rows and columns shown in the console.
- The reports are read-only: no reclamation or deletion action is offered from them.
- The dashboard build and test pipeline is green with the change.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking — this epic delivers the report.
- HLR-2 (P1): The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2): Administrators can export either report as CSV (bundled here because it is a presentation mode of the same reports surface and data).

# Document the idle and stale resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers administrator documentation for the new idle resource reporting capability in the RHOAI web console: what each report shows, how to interpret it, and how to safely reclaim the capacity it identifies.

## Scope

- A documentation topic explaining the per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) and the stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts).
- Instructions for configuring the stale-run age threshold.
- Instructions for exporting either report as CSV.
- Guidance on safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, including how to verify a resource is genuinely idle before acting.
- Clear statement of boundaries: automated reclamation/deletion and cost/chargeback calculations are not part of the feature.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, their columns, the configurable age threshold, and CSV export.
- Published documentation walks through safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, with verification guidance before acting.
- The documentation explicitly states that automated reclamation and cost/chargeback are out of scope.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented console behavior and matches what the reports actually display.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.
